report.source_text: A lumbar puncture was performed. CSF was fully transparent with 18 cells per μl (normal range: 0–5), 60% of neutrophils and 38% of lymphocytes, a positive Pandy’s reaction, a negative Nonne-Apelt reaction, 154.0 mg/dl of protein (normal range: 15–45), a normal concentration of glucose (79 mg%, normal range: 50–80), 2.7 mmol/l of lactic acid (normal range: 0.5–2.2). A latex test and aerobic and anaerobic cultures of CSF yielded negative results. The patient tested negatively for anti-CMV, anti-EBV, anti-HSV, anti-poxvirus and anti-Borrelia burgdorferi IgM antibodies. The results of other tests, including aerobic and anaerobic cultures of the blood (collected at peak fever) and urine, were also negative.

report.source_text: A pterional craniotomy was performed on the right side under general anaesthesia with the patient in a supine position. After reaching the base of the brain and evacuation of fluid from basal cisterns, the tumour’s wall was cut, and a thick yellowish fluid was drained. The tumour was separated from the right optic nerve, right ICA, optic chiasm and left optic nerve. Instead of the pituitary stalk, two thin bands were found, extending from the third ventricle and running towards the sella turcica on both sides of the tumour. After separating the tumour from those bands, it was incised slightly above the sellar diaphragm, dissected from the third ventricle wall, along the lamina terminalis, and removed. After achieving haemostasis, the dura mater was sutured and fixed to the bone and a cranioplasty was performed. A suction drain was then placed, soft tissues were closed in layers and protected with a dressing.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 7-year-old girl presented with severe headache, vomiting, muscle weakness, balance disorders, and concentration problems. Preoperative CT revealed a large cystic craniopharyngioma with acute hydrocephalus. She underwent pterional craniotomy for tumor resection, during which a thick yellowish fluid was drained from the tumor. The first 6 postoperative days were without complications. On postoperative day 7, her status rapidly deteriorated with severe headache, fever, altered consciousness, seizures, and meningeal signs. CSF analysis on day 7 showed pleocytosis (18 cells/µl, 60% neutrophils), elevated protein (154 mg/dl), elevated lactic acid (2.7 mmol/l), and negative bacterial/viral cultures. Blood, urine, and viral IgM tests were also negative for infection. She received broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy and antiepileptics. Due to increasing intracranial pressure, external drainage was placed on day 11 and removed on day 14. On day 14, meningeal symptoms and other neurological deficits persisted.

She underwent pterional craniotomy for tumor resection, during which a thick yellowish fluid was drained from the tumor. The first 6 postoperative days were without complications. On postoperative day 7, her status rapidly deteriorated with severe headache, fever, altered consciousness, seizures, and meningeal signs. CSF analysis on day 7 showed pleocytosis (18 cells/µl, 60% neutrophils), elevated protein (154 mg/dl), elevated lactic acid (2.7 mmol/l), and negative bacterial/viral cultures. Blood, urine, and viral IgM tests were also negative for infection. She received broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy and antiepileptics. Due to increasing intracranial pressure, external drainage was placed on day 11 and removed on day 14. On day 14, meningeal symptoms and other neurological deficits persisted.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with symptoms of increased intracranial pressure and a brain tumor.
Preoperative CT revealed a large cystic tumor (craniopharyngioma) with acute hydrocephalus.
Surgical resection of the craniopharyngioma involved draining 'thick yellowish fluid' from the tumor.
Rapid clinical deterioration on postoperative day 7 with symptoms consistent with meningitis (severe headache, fever, altered consciousness, seizures, meningeal signs).
CSF analysis on postoperative day 7 showed pleocytosis (18 cells/µl with 60% neutrophils), elevated protein (154 mg/dl), and elevated lactic acid (2.7 mmol/l).
CSF, blood, and urine cultures were negative for bacterial and viral pathogens.
Negative IgM antibodies for common viral causes of meningitis (CMV, EBV, HSV, poxvirus, Borrelia burgdorferi).
Microbiological examination of throat and nasal swabs revealed physiological microflora.
Meningeal symptoms persisted on postoperative day 14 despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy.
